name: elegantuvm
description: UVM-aware SystemVerilog: one-click class graph, component topology with factory overrides, config_db cross-reference, UVM lint with quick fixes, slang elaboration diagnostics and an MCP server for AI agents. Free and open source, built on slang.

uvm.filelists.description: Simulator filelists (.f) to index, e.g. ["sim/tb.f"]. Empty: every SystemVerilog file in the workspace is indexed and include paths are inferred.

uvm.uvmHome.markdownDescription: UVM installation to index (the directory containing `src/uvm_pkg.sv`). Falls back to `$UVM_HOME` when unset or when it holds no `uvm_pkg.sv`. When neither applies, the project's own `uvm_pkg.sv` is used if it has one, otherwise the Accellera UVM 1.2 bundled with the extension (see `#uvm.useBundledUvm#`).

uvm.useBundledUvm.markdownDescription: Index the Accellera UVM 1.2 library that ships with the extension. Used only when `#uvm.uvmHome#` and `$UVM_HOME` are not set and the project has no `uvm_pkg.sv` of its own. Turning it off falls back to the lightweight built-in UVM model, which cannot elaborate.

uvm.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files and folders to leave out in discovery mode, matched below each workspace folder as in `#files.exclude#`: `legacy/**`, `**/*_old.sv`. An absolute pattern matches the full path. Simulator output folders (`work`, `csrc`, `simv.daidir`, `xcelium.d`, `INCA_libs`, `obj_dir`) and `.git`, `.venv`, `node_modules` and `__pycache__` inside the workspace are always left out.

uvm.pythonPath.description: Python interpreter with pyslang and pygls installed. Supports ${workspaceFolder} and ~. Empty: auto-detect (a .venv/venv in the workspace or its parent folders, then the extension's own environment, then python3).

uvm.pipArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments for `pip install` when the extension creates its own Python environment: a package mirror (`--index-url`, `--trusted-host`) or a proxy (`--proxy`). The Linux x86_64 package first installs the wheels it ships, without any network; these arguments apply to the fallback install from the index.

uvm.lint.enabled.description: Report UVM lint findings (config_db mismatches, unregistered classes, ...).

uvm.codeLens.configDb.description: Show config_db set/get cross-references above calls.

uvm.formatter.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable Format Document and Format Selection with an optional local Verible executable. Verible emits spaces using the editor's tab size. This does not change `#editor.formatOnSave#` or the default formatter.

uvm.formatter.path.markdownDescription: Path or executable name for verible-verilog-format on the server's machine. Empty: search the server's PATH. Supports ~, environment variables and ${workspaceFolder}; relative paths use the first workspace root. This is one executable, not a shell command. An invalid explicit path does not fall back to PATH.

uvm.inlayHints.markdownDescription: Show UVM type inlay hints. VS Code's `#editor.inlayHints.enabled#` also controls their display.

uvm.inlayHintsTest.description: Test whose factory overrides appear in inlay hints. Empty: use the topology's default test.

enumDescriptions: Only when you run UVM: Elaborate Now.
After a file is saved and after the workspace is re-indexed.
Also about a second after you stop typing, without saving.
uvm.elaboration.markdownDescription: Compile and elaborate the design with slang, in a separate process, to report what a simulator's elaboration would: type errors, unknown members, wrong argument counts, missing modules or packages and the like (source `slang-elab`). It uses the same files, include directories and defines as the index, and the text of open editors. Needs a real UVM library (the bundled one is fine).

uvm.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Register the UVM MCP server (`python -m uvmls mcp`) with VS Code, so Copilot and other agents in the editor can query the testbench: classes, the topology with factory overrides, config_db, lint, elaboration, navigation. It runs as a separate process on the first workspace folder with the `uvm` settings as its flags, and reads the files on disk (unsaved editor text is not visible). See **MCP: List Servers**.

scripts.package: node scripts/fetch-verible.mjs && node scripts/bundle-server.mjs && node esbuild.mjs --production && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies && node scripts/check-notices.mjs
scripts.package:linux-x64: node scripts/fetch-verible.mjs && node scripts/fetch-wheels.mjs && node scripts/bundle-server.mjs --target linux-x64 && node esbuild.mjs --production && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --target linux-x64 && node scripts/check-notices.mjs --target linux-x64
scripts.package:all: npm run package && npm run package:linux-x64

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The UVM language server runs a Python interpreter, which may come from the workspace (.venv or uvm.pythonPath). Trust the folder to enable it.
